subject: Amendment: Tier consolidation + surge safeguard — action items
messages:
From: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@brightlayer.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Jen Wang <jen.wang@brightlayer.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversation — tier consolidation and surge protection

David / team,

Thanks again — we're starting prep for our March renewal and want to explore a model simplification that reduces ops friction between our 'Standard' and 'Surge' tiers. High level ask: can Redwood consolidate the two tiers into a single committed tier with an operational surge safeguard and a short-term price hold while we migrate workloads?

What matters to BrightLayer:
- Predictable unit pricing for 6–12 months during the migration window.
- A surge safeguard (hard cap or credits) to protect us from runaway costs during traffic spikes tied to seasonal campaigns.
- Some bridging credit to offset migration risk (we can put dollars against a short-term true-up).

I've attached our Q4 usage export so you can see burst patterns (attachment: usage_report_q4.csv).

Our timeline: prefer to finalize a term sheet by Mar 15 so procurement can issue PO by end of month.

Can you propose 1–2 practical options (price-hold + credits vs. consolidated tier + stepped true-up) and a recommended next step? Happy to do a 30-min call next week.

Best,
Alex
Alex Murphy
Head of Infrastructure, BrightLayer
Attachments: usage_report_q4.csv (CSV, 120KB)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@brightlayer.com>, Jen Wang <jen.wang@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — tier consolidation and surge protection

Alex — thanks for the clear framing and the usage export. Sharing a quick internal-first pass so we can align on commercial guardrails before we involve finance/legal.

Two pragmatic options to start the discussion:

Option 1 — 12-month price hold + conditional bridging credits
- Lock current effective rate for 12 months from renewal signing.
- Provide a one-time bridging credit of $125,000 to offset migration spikes; credit applies to overage invoices for the first 90 days.
- Implement a surge safeguard: automatic alerting at 1.8x baseline and an overage cap at 3x baseline for 30 days (after which standard overage rates apply).

Option 2 — Consolidated committed tier with stepped true-up
- Consolidate Standard + Surge into single committed tier with a baseline equal to combined current commit.
- 6-month price hold from signing.
- Stepped true-up: allow 2x burst for first 60 days, 1.5x for next 60 days; provide $100k credit if bursts exceed 2x in first 30 days.

Differences & tradeoffs:
- Option 1 gives BrightLayer longer price predictability and larger initial credit; reduces operational changes on your side.
- Option 2 reduces SKU complexity going forward but requires a shorter hold while we monitor true-up behavior.

I've attached an action-oriented draft term sheet with the two options for your review (attachment: BrightLayer_MA_plan_v3.pdf — redlineable).

Internal asks: Marissa / Priyom — can you run margin impact and confirm whether finance is comfortable with the $125k vs $100k credit scenarios? Also need legal to confirm any language we should avoid around 'hard caps' vs 'credit-backed caps'.

Alex — can we schedule a quick 30-min sync Mon/Tue next week to pick one option and get to a term sheet?

Regards,
David Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: BrightLayer_MA_plan_v3.pdf (term sheet draft, 48KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@brightlayer.com>, Jen Wang <jen.wang@brightlayer.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Feb 2027 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — tier consolidation and surge protection

Thanks, David — reviewed the draft. High level counter with specifics so we can move to a legal-ready term sheet quickly. Keeping the ask short.

Counter (recommended commercial):
- Hybrid option (preferred): 6-month price hold on current effective blended rate + $150,000 bridging credit applied to overages in months 1–3.
- Surge safeguard: implement a capped surcharge where overage billing is limited to 2x baseline for the first 60 days, then reverts to standard rates unless we mutually agree to extend. Any usage above 2x baseline in months 1–30 days gets a partial credit back ($/token credit equal to 50% of overage charge).
- Consolidation path: move to one committed tier after 90 days of monitoring; if observed monthly usage exceeds baseline by >25% for two consecutive months, trigger a true-up conversation (no automatic punitive step).

Commercial rationale: $150k credit covers estimated migration bursts based on Q4 export and keeps Redwood protected vs open-ended guarantees. This structure reduces complexity for BrightLayer while preserving Redwood's cost alignment.

Next ops steps:
- Priyom: please confirm P&L impact and suggest final credit number if margin stress is >8%.
- Irene: confirm wording for 'capped surcharge' vs 'hard cap' (we prefer credit-backed cap language).
- David: propose a 30-min review with BrightLayer Tues (Feb 2) 9:00–11:00 PT.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Murphy <alex.murphy@brightlayer.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Jen Wang <jen.wang@brightlayer.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — tier consolidation and surge protection

Hi David / Marissa / team — appreciate the fast turnaround and thoughtful options. BrightLayer prefers Marissa's hybrid counter with one tweak: extend the surge cap to 2.5x for the first 60 days (instead of 2x) given our anticipated campaign load in month 1; we accept the $150k bridging credit and the 6-month price hold.

If Redwood can provide a final term sheet reflecting the hybrid language (credit-backed cap, 6-month price hold, conditional transition to consolidated tier after 90 days of monitoring) we can route to procurement. Can you share the DocuSign link once legal has the final language?

Proposed next step: 30-min sign-off call Wed Feb 3 at 10:00 PT to review final term sheet and DocuSign flow.

Thanks — looking forward to closing.
Alex Murphy
Head of Infrastructure, BrightLayer
Attachments referenced: BrightLayer_MA_plan_v3.pdf (we reviewed)
